questions.question: Direction: In the question below is given a statement followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true, then consider the two conclusions together and decide which of them logically follows beyond a reasonable doubt from the information given in the statement. Statement: Domestic demand for steel is outpacing the supply of steel- both indigenous and Imported. Conclusions: I. Tariffs will be increased for steel imports. II. Indigenous production might be increased or quotas for steel imports might be increased.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In the question below is given a statement followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true, then consider the two conclusions together and decide which of them logically follows beyond a reasonable doubt from the information given in the statement.

Statement:

Domestic demand for steel is outpacing the supply of steel- both indigenous and Imported.

Conclusions:

I. Tariffs will be increased for steel imports.

II. Indigenous production might be increased or quotas for steel imports might be increased.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows
options.html: Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
I. Tariffs will be increased for steel imports - Raising tariffs on imports discourages imports. So, it is unlikely that such a situation will arise. Thus, such a definite conclusion can be ruled out. Hence, conclusion I does not follow.

II. Indigenous production might be increased or quotas for steel imports might be increased - The possibility of an increase in domestic production or imports to deal with the problem highlighted in the statement.

Raising quotas on imports encourages imports by allowing more imports. Similarly, indigenous production can be increased to match the demand.

Either of these or both of these actions can help deal with the issue. So, these actions might be considered to meet the domestic demand. Hence, conclusion II follows.

questions.question: Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 14 × 6 ÷ 12 + 15 - 9 = 203
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

14 × 6 ÷ 12 + 15 - 9 = 203
questions.solution:
Given statement : 14 × 6 ÷ 12 + 15 - 9 = 203

According to the question, after interchanging the given two signs and two numbers :

So,

  • Option - (1) : 15, 6, +, ÷ 

14 × 15 + 12 ÷ 6 - 9 = 203

14 × 15 + 2 - 9 = 203

210 + 2 - 9 = 203

212 - 9 = 203

203 = 203 (LHS = RHS)

  • Option - (2) : 12, 15, -, × 

14 - 6 ÷ 15 + 12 × 9 = 203

14 - 0.4 + 12 × 9 = 203

14 + 108 - 0.4 =203

112 - 0.4 = 203

111.6  ≠ 203 (LHS ≠ RHS)

  • Option - (3) : 12, 9, ÷, -

14 × 6 - 9 + 15 ÷ 12 = 203

14 × 6 - 9 + 1.25 = 203

84 + 1.25 - 9 = 203

85.25 - 9 = 203

76.25  ≠ 203 (LHS ≠ RHS)

  • Option - (4) : 14, 6, ÷, × 

6 ÷ 14 × 12 + 15 - 9 = 203

0.43 × 12 + 15 - 9 = 203

5 + 15 - 9 = 203

20 - 9  ≠ 203 (LHS ≠ RHS)

11 ≠ 203 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, "Option - (1)" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (13, 43, 177) (9, 31,129)
questions.questionHtml:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)

(13, 43, 177)

(9, 31,129)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:-

(First number × 3) + 4 = Second number 

(Second number × 4) + 5 = Third number.

(13, 43, 177) → (13 × 3) + 4 = 39 + 4 = 43 and (43 × 4) + 5 = 172 + 5 = 177

And,

(9, 31, 129) → (9 × 3) + 4 = 27 + 4 = 31 and (31 × 4) + 5 = 124 + 5 = 129

Similarly,

(29, 91, 369) → (29 × 3) + 4 = 87 + 4 = 91 and (91 × 4) + 5 = 364 + 5 = 369

Hence, the correct answer is "(29, 91, 369)".

Statements: All sachets are bags. Some bags are clocks. No clock is a toaster. Conclusions: I. Some toasters are clocks. II. No sachet is a toaster. Ill. Some bags are sachets.
